findings.title: A grill-closed finding is both refused (agent) and allowed (grill), though the grill is an agent

disposed as a spec fix `--by grill`

sources.situation: the grill agent (A-2) settles DF-1 in a delegated session, removes it from `## Deferred`, and records the disposition `--by grill`. FR-16 refuses it because an agent recorded it. AC-22 and the closing table accept it, since `grill` is a distinct value from `agent`. A plain agent that passes `--by grill` after deleting the DF line also gets through. The same actor gets two outcomes, and the spec never says how `grill` is told apart from `agent`.

findings.reason: FR-16 allows closing "through a grill session" yet refuses "a disposition recorded by an agent", and A-2 says the grill is an agent. The closing table separates `grill` from `agent` only by the `--by` value. Nothing in the spec says who may pass `--by grill`, so a plain agent can pass it after deleting the DF line. Q1's answer ("Agents can never close one") doesn't settle this either.
findings.note: the human: --by grill means the human answered; a delegated session leaves the finding for the human (FR-16)

sources.situation: the glossary bans "reimbursement" and an AC contains `reimbursement-free`. A hyphen is an ordinary word boundary, so `reimbursement` is a whole word inside `reimbursement-free`. An implementer following FR-19 literally would fail AC-21, and the test would show it. The AC adds behaviour that the FR it is derived from does not state.

findings.reason: FR-19 says "whole word" with no hyphen rule, and a hyphen is an ordinary boundary, so `reimbursement` is a whole word in `reimbursement-free`. AC-21 still requires that case to pass. Nothing else in the spec (glossary, Decisions, Non-goals, Q5) defines the boundary.

sources.situation: A deferred finding is disposed as a spec fix `--by grill` once DF-1 has left `## Deferred`. The disposition is not `by: human`, FR-16 allows it, and the finding is no longer open, so FR-17 lets the jury approve. SC-1 says that spec must not reach an approved verdict, because its deferred point has no human disposition. The key entity and US-3 still say "closed only by the human". Meanwhile the Decisions say `--by` is "the caller's word" and the spec does not check that the human answered, so the one path an agent could abuse is the one SC-1 appears to forbid.

A delegated agent removes the DF line and its tag from the spec, then disposes the open finding as a spec fix `--by grill`. FR-20 is satisfied, the finding closes, and FR-17 no longer blocks, so the verdict can be approved with no human disposition. SC-1 says this cannot happen. The non-goal admits that `--by` is only the caller's word, so the same bypass exists with `--by human`.

A finding is closed `--by grill` as a spec fix, and the DF is removed from `## Deferred`. The finding is now disposed, but not by `--by human`. SC-1 reads "no human disposition", so a reader could count this case as a failure of the criterion. FR-17 only blocks approval while a finding is open. It says nothing about a DF whose finding was never collected.

a finding is disposed `--by grill` as a spec fix. A grill session closes it, with no `by: human` disposition, and FR-17 then lets the verdict be approved. SC-1 says a point with no human disposition must not reach approval, so SC-1's success test fails while every FR and AC passes. A finding can also be open after its DF has been removed from `## Deferred`, and no AC says what the verdict does then.
